terms.gloss: land, as against sea and sky
evidence: Caes. BC 2.1: reliqua quarta est, quae aditum habeat ā terrā
terms.comment: The same word as earth and soil (see dirt). By land is the plain ablative, terrā (Cic. iter terrā petere, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 56; Sall. Cat. 13.3 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A fixed pair, very frequent (Lewis & Short); et terrā et marī is also classical.

terms.gloss: a piece of land, a field

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Verg., Ov.
evidence: Ov. Met. 1.291: jamque mare et tellūs nūllum discrīmen habēbant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A word that belongs almost wholly to poetry; prose says terra (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: seeing land after a long tossing at sea

phrases.latin: vēnerat ad mē māter pietāte fortis, terrā marīque mē sequēns
phrases.english: my mother had come to me, strong in her devotion, following me by land and sea

phrases.latin: jamque mare et tellūs nūllum discrīmen habēbant
phrases.english: and now sea and land were not to be told apart

phrases.latin: fundit humō facilem vīctum jūstissima tellūs
phrases.english: the earth, most just, pours an easy living from the ground

sources: Lewis & Short: ager
Lewis & Short: terra
